title: Sum in a Matrix
statement:
You start with a score of 0 and the integer matrix `nums`. Repeat the following round until no numbers are left:

1. Take one largest value out of every row (if a row holds several copies of its maximum, any one of them may go).
2. Among the values taken out in this round, add the biggest one to your score.

Return the score once the matrix is empty.
constraints: All rows of nums have the same length
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the rounds literally means searching every row for its maximum again and again. But each row simply gives up its values from largest to smallest, so round `k` removes the `k`-th largest value of every row. Sort each row in decreasing order first and round `k` becomes column `k`: the score is the sum of the column maxima.

## Approach

1. Sort every row of `nums` in decreasing order.
2. Start `score` at 0.
3. For each column index `col`, find `largest`, the biggest value in that column across all rows.
4. Add `largest` to `score`; after the last column, return `score`.

## Example 1, step by step

The rows sorted in decreasing order are `[7,2,1]`, `[6,4,2]`, `[6,5,3]` and `[3,2,1]`.

- `col = 0`: values 7, 6, 6, 3, so `largest = 7` and `score = 7`.
- `col = 1`: values 2, 4, 5, 2, so `largest = 5` and `score = 12`.
- `col = 2`: values 1, 2, 3, 1, so `largest = 3` and `score = 15`.

The answer is `15`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n log n) for sorting the `m` rows of length `n`; the column scan adds only O(m · n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort, since the rows are sorted in place.

## Pitfalls

- Sort with a numeric comparator; the default `sort()` compares numbers as strings, so `[10, 9]` would be ordered wrongly.
- Sort each row on its own. Sorting columns or the whole matrix mixes values between rows and breaks the rounds.
- Ties do not matter: whichever copy of a maximum is removed, the same value goes into that round.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row` | one row of `nums`, sorted largest first |
| `score` | running total of the round maxima |
| `col` | the round number, which is also a column index after sorting |
| `largest` | the biggest value removed in round `col` |

narration.2: Each row will give up its values from largest to smallest, so line them up that way.
narration.3: Sort the row in decreasing order with a numeric comparator.
narration.5: No rounds have been played yet, so the score starts at zero.
narration.6: After sorting, round col removes exactly the values in column col.
narration.7: Values are never negative, so zero is a safe starting maximum for this round.
narration.8: Look at the value each row gives up in this round.
narration.9: Keep the biggest value removed in this round.
narration.11: Only the round's biggest removed value counts towards the score.
narration.13: Every column has been processed, so the matrix is empty; return the score.
